subject.title: [Feature Request] 浏览器使用后自动关闭机制

question: Should OpenClaw treat browser shutdown as an automatic agent/session lifecycle responsibility, or keep browser reuse as the default and expose only an explicit cleanup/idle policy?
rationale: The issue proposes several materially different policies, and choosing the default determines compatibility for existing Chrome/CDP workflows and whether a new configuration surface is warranted.

options.title: Define session-bound cleanup
options.body: Close browser resources when the owning agent/session reaches a clear terminal boundary while retaining reuse during active multi-step work.

options.title: Add opt-in idle cleanup
options.body: Keep current reuse behavior by default and add a narrowly documented idle-timeout or explicit cleanup policy for operators who need resource reclamation.

options.title: Keep explicit control only
options.body: Retain the current browser lifecycle and document the supported explicit stop/heartbeat cleanup workflow if automatic teardown would undermine valid reuse.

recommendation.title: Define session-bound cleanup
recommendation.body: Close browser resources when the owning agent/session reaches a clear terminal boundary while retaining reuse during active multi-step work.

likelyOwner.reason: A browser-lifecycle history pass is needed to route the product decision to the contributor(s) who own the current CDP lifecycle.
